Baseline Behavior (BB)
Baseline Behavior refers to the standard user behavior utilized for anomaly detection in relation to video replies.

Geo-handler (GH)
The Geo-handler is a module responsible for routing features based on user region, particularly in ensuring EEA-specific exposure allocation.

General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
The GDPR is a regulation governing data protection and privacy in the European Union and the European Economic Area, implementing strict rules on processing personal data.<SEP>The GDPR mandates principles governing data protection and privacy for individuals within the EU, applicable during the trial.

Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065)
The Digital Services Act is a legislative framework that imposes obligations on hosting service providers operating within the EU/EEA, particularly regarding the management of user-generated content.

Digital Services Act
The Digital Services Act is a specific regulation within the EU that imposes obligations on hosting service providers, including rules related to transparency, user redress, and risk assessments.<SEP>The Digital Services Act outlines obligations for online platforms regarding content moderation, transparency, and user protection in the EU.

EEA
The EEA (European Economic Area) is the region where the video reply functionality will be rolled out, encompassing multiple European countries.<SEP>The European Economic Area (EEA) encompasses EU countries and allows for the implementation of region-specific functionalities and regulations.

Video Reply Functionality
The video reply functionality is a feature being trialed specifically for users in the EEA, focusing on user-generated video content and analytics.

Articles 14–16
Articles 14–16 of the Digital Services Act outline obligations for hosting service providers to manage illegal content and implement notice-and-action mechanisms.<SEP>Articles 14–16 of the Digital Services Act stipulate the obligations for hosting services regarding notice-and-action mechanisms for illegal content.

Article 15 / Article 24
Article 15 includes transparency reporting obligations for providers of intermediary services as stated in the Digital Services Act.<SEP>Article 15 outlines transparency reporting obligations, while Article 24 addresses related content moderation responsibilities under the Digital Services Act.

Article 20
Article 20 mandates the creation of an internal complaint-handling system for users to challenge content moderation decisions.<SEP>Article 20 of the Digital Services Act pertains to internal complaint-handling systems for users to challenge content moderation decisions.

DSA
The Digital Services Act (DSA) builds on prior recommendations regarding illegal online content and includes frameworks for enforcement and compliance.

SCCs
SCCs (Standard Contractual Clauses) are contractual provisions used to ensure compliance with data protection requirements for cross-border data transfers.

Articles 33–37
Articles 33–37 establish the designation threshold and obligations for Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) under the Digital Services Act.<SEP>Articles 33–37 outline the obligations for very large online platforms, including risk assessments and audits.

Article 27
Article 27 addresses transparency obligations regarding recommender systems and the documentation needed for algorithmic decision-making.<SEP>Article 27 requires transparency concerning the parameters used in recommender systems to moderate content.

GDPR
GDPR is a regulation in EU law on data protection and privacy, applicable to individuals within the European Union and the European Economic Area.<SEP>GDPR is a regulation that governs the protection of personal data and privacy in the European Union.

Commission Recommendation
Commission Recommendation pertains to prior guidelines and frameworks regarding content regulation and impacts the DSA's implementation.

Consent
Consent is a lawful basis for processing personal data, where individuals must agree to the use of their data.

Dec 2023
Dec 2023 marks a significant period regarding DSA enforcement activities for platforms involved in video content hosting.

Art. 4(5)
Art. 4(5) defines 'Pseudonymisation' within the context of data protection regulations, clarifying strategies to protect personal data.

Art. 46(2)(c)
Art. 46(2)(c) refers to a specific article in legal texts which discusses conditions related to data processing and transfer requirements under GDPR.

Art. 5(1)(c)
Art. 5(1)(c) outlines the principle of data minimization, which mandates that personal data must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary.

Art. 5(1)(e)
Art. 5(1)(e) states the principle of storage limitation, indicating that personal data must not be stored longer than necessary.

Personal Data
Personal data refers to information that relates to an identified or identifiable individual, which must be collected and processed lawfully under regulations like GDPR.

Art. 6(1)(a)
Art. 6(1)(a) specifies that processing personal data is lawful if the subject has given consent.

Art. 8
Art. 8 sets special rules for obtaining consent from children regarding data processing.

Art. 6(1)(f)
Art. 6(1)(f) allows for lawful processing on the basis of legitimate interests.

Third Countries
Third Countries are nations outside the EU/EEA that may require specific safeguards for personal data transfers.

DSA Enforcement Activity
DSA Enforcement Activity refers to the implementation and action taken regarding compliance and enforcement of Digital Services Act regulations.

Standard Contractual Clauses
Standard Contractual Clauses refer to pre-approved contract terms used to ensure adequate protection in the transfer of personal data to third countries.

Regulations
Regulations refer to legal directives that dictate the obligations of online platforms related to content moderation and data protection.

Trial Run of Video Replies in EU
The trial run of video replies is a functionality being tested specifically for users in the European Economic Area (EEA).

Baseline Behavior
Baseline Behavior is a standard used for anomaly detection, collecting telemetry and analytics during the trial run.

Obligations
Obligations are the specific legal requirements that online service providers must fulfill under the Digital Services Act and GDPR.

Geo-handler
The Geo-handler is a module responsible for routing features based on user region, ensuring compliance with regional restrictions.

Directive
Directive refers to a legal instrument used in the EU that requires member states to achieve a particular outcome while allowing them to devise their own laws.

Data Minimisation
Data minimisation is a principle under GDPR that requires personal data to be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary for processing.

Art.5(1)(c)
Art.5(1)(c) outlines the principle of data minimisation, specifying limitations on the amount of personal data collected.

Art.5(1)(e)
Art.5(1)(e) addresses storage limitation requirements for personal data under GDPR.

Art.6(1)(a)/(f)
Art.6(1)(a)/(f) outlines lawful bases for processing personal data, including consent and legitimate interests.

Commission Recommendation / DSA preparatory materials
This document provides guidance and context for the Digital Services Act (DSA) obligations and enforcement.

Art.4(5)
Art.4(5) defines pseudonymisation in the context of personal data processing under GDPR.

Art.8
Art.8 governs child-consent rules in data processing under GDPR.

Art.46(2)(c)
Art.46(2)(c) provides safeguards for international data transfers under the GDPR.

Art.35
Art.35 requires Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for high-risk processing activities.

DSA VLOP Enforcement Dec2023
This event highlights the enforcement activities noted in December 2023 concerning platforms providing video content under DSA regulations.

Data Protection Impact Assessment
Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is a process required under Art.35 of GDPR for assessing the impact of high-risk data processing.

International Data Transfers
International Data Transfers involve moving personal data outside the European Economic Area, which is regulated under Art.46 of GDPR.

High-risk Processing
High-risk processing refers to data processing activities that pose significant risks to the rights and freedoms of individuals.

Child-consent Rules
Child-consent Rules dictate how consent should be obtained for processing the personal data of minors as outlined in Art.8 of GDPR.
